text:
Fabian Zetterlund is having one of the stranger shooting seasons you'll see. The Senators forward has 2 goals on 6.7 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 3.7% on 54 shots, against a talent range of roughly 10% to 14%. He scored 17 last season.

Everything else says he's helping. Ottawa wins 63.7% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, 12 points better than without him. He hits (53 of them), skates well (77th percentile top speed) and has 9 assists, so the points haven't dried up. Only the finishing has.

Our numbers treat that as a bounce, not a decline: goals tend to follow chances, and our range still has him around 14 by season's end. The sting is in wins added, where his goals rank near the bottom of the league because the ones he should have had never came. Ottawa has won seven of its last ten anyway. When Zetterlund's shots start going in, a good team gets a scorer it hasn't had yet.
headline: Zetterlund keeps getting looks, not goals
